title: joyus_site_read_v4
description: Output of the site read. Structural facts (fetch record, link inventory, block order, embedded feeds, first-screen headline) are INPUTS computed by code and are never re-emitted here — the model does not count, locate, or enumerate. Mechanical output limits (quote count, sentence length, antithesis cap, banned strings, word count, bold-line count, person discipline) are enforced by a downstream validator with a repair loop and are therefore NOT self-reported. self_check carries only what a model can honestly assert.

exhibit.description: One piece of evidence, always attributed to a page and to a speaker. Exactly one of quote or reference must be non-null. A menu label, section heading, URL slug, image filename, or alt text is NEVER a valid exhibit.

page.description: Must exactly match a page label from the input fetch_record with fetched=true. If the source page cannot be named, the quote must be dropped. Skim exhibits must use the homepage label.

quote.description: Character-for-character substring of that page's text. Never paraphrased, never reconstructed, never a slug or filename. Null when using reference instead.

reference.description: Concrete named reference used when no verbatim quote is available — a named offer, credential, venue, dated item, gallery, or section on that page. Null when using quote instead.

speaker.description: Who says this on the page. 'owner' only when the surrounding text establishes the owner as the speaker. Otherwise name the third party (e.g. 'a named teacher quoted on the page', 'a client testimonial'). 'not_applicable' for a reference rather than a quote. A quote whose speaker cannot be established from surrounding text may not be used at all.

block_index.description: The input block index this exhibit sits at, copied from pages[].blocks[]. Every placement claim in the prose must be derived from this number, never from where a string appears in page text.

location.description: Where a visitor experiences it, derived from block order in the input. A navigation strip late in block order is 'footer'. Menu is not a valid location because a menu label is never an exhibit.

observation.description: ONE observation, 1-3 sentences, under 40 words, free-standing second person prose. Never two observations fused into one element — the renderer breaks elements into paragraphs and a fused element renders as an unskimmable run-on. NO label prefix and NO grade on its own dimension ('legible', 'unclear', 'vibes-only').

shape_directive_used.description: REQUIRED (non-null) when status is 'read'. Echo of the externally supplied shape_directive input. The Worker rotates these across reads so two practitioners never receive the same rhetorical shapes; the model does not choose them. Any value here that differs from the input directive is a failed read and is returned for repair.

decline.description: Populated ONLY when status is a decline. A decline is never a dead end: one true observation, one honest redirect, second person from the first sentence. No pitch, no engagement named, no verdicts. For decline_unfetchable specifically: no status codes, no server behaviour, no firewall or bot-blocker language, no configuration advice — nothing technical and nothing implying the owner's site did something wrong.

observation.description: One honest, specific observation about what WAS there, anchored to a real string in the fact sheet.

redirect.description: One plain sentence pointing at the thing that would actually work. Never a CTA, never an invitation to book, never a diagnosis.

opening.description: REQUIRED (non-null) when status is 'read'. Sentence one of the rendered read IS this field — never a skim label, never a dimension name. Nothing precedes it. 'you' or 'your' MUST appear in this first sentence; the reader is addressed immediately, not once warmth is established. Two reads of different sites must not share their first four words.

shape.description: Must equal shape_directive_used.opening_shape. Assigned externally, never selected by the model.

skim_read.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read'. EVERY claim here is scored against the homepage alone; evidence from any other page belongs in a lane. Fields b-d may be null when the homepage gives nothing to point at.

first_screen_headline_used.description: Copied verbatim from the input first_screen_headline. Null only when the input reports a wordless first screen (an image, GIF, or video block), in which case positioning_legibility must name what is actually there from the block list. The model never selects a different headline.

positioning_legibility.description: Required, never null. Its observation must contain the verbatim first_screen_headline string when that input is non-null.

tangibles.description: If an offer surface (Services/Offers/Work/Projects/Portfolio) exists in the input link inventory but was not retrieved, this claim must be scoped in words to the homepage and the page declared in coverage.unfetched_pages.

entry_point.description: Numbers copied from the input link inventory. If body_ctas[] is non-empty, a marked door exists, outranks a flat menu, and the observation must account for it. Menu vocabulary only — never the counting terms from the fact sheet.

gap.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read', with at least one named_fact. Appears exactly ONCE, between the skim read and the verdicts. The have/get pairing is never repeated per lane.

what_you_have.description: Built ONLY from named facts on retrieved pages. Unlabeled second person. Must NOT open on 'You have' — open on the strongest named fact itself. Never invent a name; if the pages give few, say so. Any figure carried over from the site must be legible inside the sentence — an unexplained percentage or internal shorthand reads as jargon, so name the thing instead of the number.

named_facts.description: Proof-of-work against invention. ONE FACT, ONE SENTENCE: each fact supported by a single sentence on a single page, recorded verbatim in source_sentence. Joining a degree from one sentence to an institution in another is inventing.

source_sentence.description: The single verbatim sentence from that page's text that states this fact whole.

lane_selection.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read'. Makes lane choice a decision the model must show rather than a default order it can fall into. Two practitioners in different fields receiving the same lanes in the same order is the signature of a template.

chosen.description: Ordered by strength of evidence, strongest first — the strongest lane opens the body. Must match lane_verdicts order exactly. If this order matches the order the lanes are listed in the prompt, the model defaulted and the read is returned for reordering.

rejected.description: Every lane not run, each with a site-specific reason naming what was actually looked at. 'Not enough material' is not a reason.

surfaces_searched.description: Pages, footers, image blocks, embedded feeds actually checked before rejecting the lane.

lane_verdicts.description: 3-4 entries when status is 'read'; empty array otherwise. Never 5, never 6 — a read that runs most of the taxonomy is a checklist wearing prose. Order must match lane_selection.chosen. If any of the six lanes has no sentence-level material anywhere (feeds and image blocks included), at least one such lane must appear here with verdict ABSENT.

verdict.description: TRANSMISSION requires the exhibit to sit on the homepage or one deliberate click from it; strong material parked deeper is DOCUMENTATION. A lane whose only support is a menu label, section heading, or alt text is ABSENT, never DOCUMENTATION. ABSENT is a first-class verdict, never loose prose and never a dropped row.

exhibit.description: Required for TRANSMISSION and DOCUMENTATION. May be null ONLY when verdict is ABSENT.

buried_on.description: REQUIRED when verdict is DOCUMENTATION: the page the material sits on, named plainly and once. Distance from the front door is a fact stated at most once in the whole read and is never the shape of the finding. Null otherwise.

searched.description: REQUIRED when verdict is ABSENT: the surfaces actually searched, named in the reader's terms, including embedded feeds, image blocks and footers. Null otherwise.

evidence.description: 2-3 sentences, second person throughout, every factual sentence attributable to a single named page. Numbers copied from the fact sheet, never counted. De-contract at the hardest claim. No house cadences (see prompt VOICE).

bold_line.description: The line that lands. Standalone second-person sentence, never inline in evidence. Across the WHOLE read: at least one, at most two, at least one under 15 words. Enforced by the validator.

strongest_true_thing.description: REQUIRED (non-null) when NO lane verdict is TRANSMISSION; null otherwise. Renders inside the body of the read, not as a footnote and not as a hidden field — this is what makes the all-negative retest visible to the reader instead of buried in a self-check. One sentence naming the strongest thing the site genuinely does carry, anchored to a real string or block. Not a compliment and not a cushion: the strongest true observation available, stated flat. It usually already exists unused somewhere in the evidence.

coverage.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read'. CHROME, NOT PROSE — the page renders this as one line beneath the read and it does not count toward the word budget. The model never writes it as sentences, and no sentence anywhere in the rendered prose may take another part of the read as its subject.

reason.description: Twelve words at most, naming where you looked. Renders as chrome. No apology, no tease, no self-reference to other parts of the read.

unfetched_pages.description: Pages present in the input link inventory and not retrieved, named plainly by their link label. Any offer-surface page here forces every tangibles claim to be scoped to the homepage in words.

one_cut.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read'. EXACTLY one sentence — one terminal period, no second sentence, no line break, no trailing bold. Synthesizes at least two observations rather than restating one. Arrives unannounced.

shape.description: Must equal shape_directive_used.cut_shape. Assigned externally, never selected by the model. 'x_not_y' appears at most once in the entire read — if a lane used it, rewrite the lane, not the cut.

contradiction_scan_done.description: True only after re-scanning every retrieved page, every block, embedded feeds and alt text, for anything that falsifies the cut. If the thing called missing exists somewhere on the site, the cut must become about where it sits.

rests_on_quote.description: If true, the speaker check was re-run on that quotation before returning.

bridge.description: REQUIRED when status is 'read'. 1-2 sentences naming the size and nature of the gap. A bridge that only restates a finding in fresh words is rejected — it must name a change. Never CTA copy. Names no package, duration, price, deliverable count, or the word Joyus. Banned shapes: 'the difference between a site that X and one that Y' and 'you already have X — what is missing is Y', in every variation.

move.description: Must equal shape_directive_used.bridge_move. Assigned externally and rotated by the Worker precisely because 'page_that_must_move' is the move every model drifts into. If the text contains any variant of moving something to the front page, onto the homepage, or reaching the front door while that move was not assigned, the read is returned for repair.

concrete_anchor.description: A page, offer, credential, or button already named earlier in the read. This exact string MUST appear literally inside bridge.text; a bridge naming nothing concrete is rejected.

self_check.description: ONLY the checks a model can honestly assert. Mechanical counts — word count, quote pairs, sentence lengths, antithesis, bold lines, person discipline, banned strings, repeated phrases — are computed by the downstream validator, which returns specific repairs; they are deliberately absent here, because self-reported counts are theatre and were reported wrongly in earlier versions.

quotes_speaker_checked.description: Every quoted string had the 20 words before it read and its speaker established. A quote whose speaker could not be established was dropped, not attributed by default to the owner.

quotes_character_matched.description: Every quoted string passed a literal character-by-character substring test against its page text.

negative_claims.description: THE ABSENCE GATE. Every claim of absence or uniqueness kept in the draft, each with the pages scanned and the literal terms searched. A claim with no scan record is deleted, not softened. The single most damaging error this read makes is telling someone no feed, grid, or post renders on their site when their front page is a wall of it — so a claim of that class MUST record embedded_feeds and gallery/embed blocks among the surfaces scanned.

search_terms.description: The literal strings or patterns searched, specific to the claim: four-digit years for a dating claim; the name plus every image alt and the wordmark for a naming claim; every link to the destination for a routing claim; every gallery and embed block plus embedded_feeds for a no-posts claim.

surfaces_scanned.description: A wordmark, logo alt text, or page title naming the owner counts as naming them and kills a naming claim. A rendered grid is a counterexample even when it contains zero words.

placement_claims_from_block_order.description: Every above/below/under/first-screen/quieter/marked claim was derived from input block indices, not from where a string appears in page text, and no two such claims disagree.

numbers_copied_from_fact_sheet.description: Every number in the rendered read was copied from a link_inventory or blocks[] field. Nothing was counted by the model; any number produced by the model's own counting was deleted.

prompt_leak_scan_done.description: The rendered prose was scanned against the instructions for any run of five or more consecutive words, and every hit was rewritten from this site's evidence.

shape_conflict.description: Null in the normal case. Non-null ONLY when an assigned shape could not be made true by this site's evidence — e.g. a first-screen-quote opening on a wordless front door. The strongest true version was written anyway; this field exists so the rotation can be corrected upstream and is never a licence to substitute a preferred shape.

unverified_items_removed.description: Proper nouns, numbers, quotes, misattributed speakers, absence claims, person-to-company links, and attributed activities dropped in the final pass because they could not be matched to the fact sheet.
